instruction.name: xvmaddwod.q.du
instruction.description: Multiply the odd-positioned unsigned 64-bit elements in `b` and the corresponding unsigned 64-bit elements in `c`, extending both to 128-bit, and add the product to the 128-bit elements in `a`.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr2, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr3, $r4
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 100000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 20 --init 'li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr2, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr3, $r4' --asm 'xvmaddwod.q.du $xr0, $xr1, $xr2'

throughput.notes: `vd` is an accumulator, so a lane can only issue once per latency. The earlier 8-lane body measured 0.8725 CPI purely from that feedback (8 lanes against a 7-cycle latency); with 30 independent accumulators and two shared sources the unit reaches two instructions per cycle.

notes: Every source-to-result path is recorded separately; vd is read as the accumulator.
